ledger.note: 1816: Duke Ernest takes possession of the Lichtenberg lands on the Nahe. The land was given at the Congress of Vienna 'at first under the name of Herrschaft Baumholder' and 'the possession was made official' on 11 September 1816. The page says 'The future Lichtenberger lands became part of the Département de la Sarre in 1798' (French until Napoleon's defeat; before that mostly Palatinate-Zweibrücken, St. Wendel Electoral Trier) but names no holder between Napoleon's fall and the 1816 grant, so the counterpart is 'nobody' (reviewer eu-20-k correction); the infobox starts the principality in 1815.
1819: the territory becomes the Principality of Lichtenberg. 'on 6 March 1819, the area would be renamed as the Principality of Lichtenberg.' Cliopatria's row starts in 1820.

notes:
Page budget 1 of 1-2 used (Principality of Lichtenberg).
CLIOPATRIA ROW. Years 1820-1827 against the page's 1816-1834 (possession 1816, renamed 1819, sold 15 August 1834) and area 179 km2 against 537 km2: the shape is a single cell reaching Baumholder that omits the capital Sankt Wendel. This dossier extends the shape to the page's years (new keyframes 1816-1819 and 1828-1834) and adds a 12 km radius around Sankt Wendel. 'Sankt Wendel' is not in the gazetteer (gazetteer_names_needed).
PREDECESSOR. The page says the lands 'became part of the Département de la Sarre in 1798' and stayed French until Napoleon's defeat (before 1798 mostly Palatinate-Zweibrücken, St. Wendel under Electoral Trier), but it names no holder for 1814/15-1816 (the Allied provisional administration), so predecessors is empty and the 1816 counterpart is 'nobody'; first-french-empire is the holder to 1814 (reviewer eu-20-k correction: the draft said the page was silent).
OWNER. The page calls it an exclave of Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld (1816-1826) and Saxe-Coburg and Gotha (1826-1834); Cliopatria's saxe-coburg-and-gotha row is 1836-1839 only and duchy-of-saxe-coburg-saalfeld has its own dossier. The principality is drawn as a state of its own, as Cliopatria does, not as a vassal of the duchy.
